Figure 1 displays a line graph illustrating the training loss of various LLaMA models over the number of training tokens. The graph includes four series, each representing a different model size: LLaMA 7B, LLaMA 13B, LLaMA 33B, and LLaMA 65B. The LLaMA 7B series starts at the highest point and ends at approximately 1.8, while the LLaMA 65B series starts lowest and ends at around 1.6. caption: Figure 2: Evolution of performance on question answering and common sense reasoning during training.
description:
Figure: Six line graphs showing the evolution of performance on various question answering and common sense reasoning tasks during the training of LLaMA models. Each graph represents a different dataset: TriviaQA, HellaSwag, NaturalQuestions, SQuAD, WinoGrande, and PIQA. The x-axis represents the number of tokens processed during training, ranging from 0 to 1500 billion. The y-axis represents accuracy, ranging from 0 to 85. Each line corresponds to a different LLaMA model size, labeled as 7B, 13B, 33B, 65B, and Chinchilla.

Description: The graphs show the performance of LLaMA models of varying sizes on six different datasets. The Chinchilla model consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all datasets, followed by the 65B, 33B, 13B, and 7B models. The accuracy generally increases with the number of tokens processed, indicating that larger models benefit more from extended training.
